103: Lowercase, emotionally evasive city scenes in long blocks; overexplains practical details, loses the thread, occasionally doubles a word or omits an apostrophe. Some sessions are flat complaints rather than stories.
104: Practical, methodical first-person explanations that get sidetracked into work or arguments. Longer sentences with misplaced commas and occasional technical spelling slips; restrained emotion, little dialogue decoration.
105: Headlong action with abrupt reversals, shouted words and physical confusion. Frequent missing commas, occasional letter reversals and forward corrections; some very fast long sessions, some stalled scraps.
106: Matter-of-fact space-worker fiction, long exasperated sentences and practical bodily detail. Occasional omitted words or tense drift; switches between dull chores and dangerous technical failures without announcing a twist.
107: Plain, literal third-person workplace narratives with repetitive nouns and awkward transitions. Generally correct spelling, occasional agreement errors; imperfect plot starts and unresolved factual details rather than lyrical endings.
108: Claustrophobic horror drafts from an uncertain narrator: accumulated sensory details, revisions of what was just claimed, oddly specific fears. Usually one dense block; occasional fragments, dropped words and a few misspellings.
109: Plain outdoor narratives with long practical detours, uncertain animal knowledge and badly connected sentences. Uneven spelling (especially unfamiliar words), little figurative language; repeats directions or quantities while working out a scene.
110: Talkative first-person social comedy, parenthetical detours without tidy setup/punchline, self-contradiction and badly timed explanations. Common-word typos and missed apostrophes appear in bursts; occasional short dialogue exchanges.
111: Observant field-note fiction with precise physical detail, uncertain identification and associative reasoning. Mostly correct spelling but unfinished comparisons, repeated qualifiers and occasional clipped fragments; mixes quiet scenes, anger and plain failed observations.
112: Industrial robot scenes written as terse actions, simple dialogue and incomplete technical reasoning. Abrupt sentences, few metaphors; occasional longer cause-and-effect runons and pragmatic corrections. Sparse intentional dialogue breaks.
113: Direct family-and-food storytelling with overlapping speech, opinions and practical interruptions. Loose punctuation, occasional repeated words and cooking misspellings; alternates confident long runs with brief beginnings that go nowhere.
114: Overexcited fantasy improvisation, earnest about absurd magical rules and poor at keeping track of them. Chatty run-ons, inconsistent tense, repeated starts, occasional misspellings; mixes long overstuffed scenes with abandoned premises.
115: Phone-typed urban scenes in a single flowing block, casual contractions, missing apostrophes, occasional swapped letters, doubled words and abrupt attention shifts. Compressed dialogue and patchy scene-setting; varying effort and frequent early stops.
116: Earnest, sometimes overworked descriptions in close third person; reaches for a comparison, abandons it, slips tense and repeats adjectives. Some drafts remain description or planning, others turn physically strange; uneven paragraphing, sparing spelling errors.
117: Blunt comic monologues with needless qualifications, petty grievances and poorly sustained logic. One long paragraph most days, occasional list or dialogue, ordinary spelling but rushed repeated words; some complaints never become stories.
118: Tired night-worker realism: direct physical actions, uneventful stretches, occasional suspicion and blunt half-dialogue. Mostly correct spelling with small omissions/repeats when attention drifts; low-key emotion, no required revelation at the end.
119: Speculative idea experiments with plain explanations that often outrun their own logic. Fast associative worldbuilding, occasional misspellings and forward amendments, little sentimentality; alternates ambitious scenes, miniature premises and conspicuous failures to solve an idea.
120: Hurried lowercase interpersonal fiction, emotionally inconsistent narrators and lots of forward corrections. Writer-specific mistyping, skipped words and doubled words in bursts, unfinished thoughts, occasional bare dialogue or an actual list; rough ordinary scenes as well as imaginative false starts.
